results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
All 41 aligned summaries match the controlling ideas of p01-p41 in spec order; the three introduction callouts match no spec paragraph.

Marked units checked: p11 (definition plus terminology note) and p19 (customer data plus fee column, unified by its opening and 'Both details show...') hold one controlling idea; p13 and p39 fail separately.

results.draft_locus: What Changes When the Provider Sells: Stripe Managed Payments ¶1
results.quote: Managed Payments is Stripe's merchant-of-record product for digital goods. Stripe's pricing page (n.d., accessed November 2026) lists "3.5% per successful Managed Payments transaction in addition to Payments fees". It says the tax service covers "more than 75 countries" where the documentation says "more than 80"; I use the documentation's figure. The release history is in Stripe's own pages.
results.finding: The paragraph carries two ideas (the fee with a 75-vs-80 aside, and an eight-step release history); the outliner needed two summaries. The spec's p13 controlling idea itself joins the price and the full release history in one paragraph.

results.draft_locus: What to Take Away ¶4
results.quote: Seen from this chapter, every chapter of Part VI was about one document.
results.finding: The paragraph holds the part-level invoice synthesis, a recap of the 1 October and 1 November renewal incidents with Keel's K1 and K5, and a course of action; the outliner needed two summaries. The spec's p39 controlling idea and the conclusion's synthesis/callback/takeaway require all of it in one paragraph.
Every body paragraph p01-p38, p40, p41 traces to S1-S5 or to the introduction/hand-off; p39 fails separately.

results.draft_locus: What to Take Away ¶4
results.quote: On 1 October its renewal job hit a rate limit and 7,900 renewals ran a day late; on 1 November a retry under a new idempotency key charged 1,840 members twice, and €71,300 was refunded.
results.finding: The renewal incidents and Keel's K1/K5 repair trace to the post's role (closing Part VI), not to any supporting claim S1-S5 about merchant of record; both flow readers read it as unrelated to the chapter's decision. The spec assigns the part's closing to this paragraph.
Evidence in p01, p05-p11, p13-p21, p23-p34, p39 is followed or framed by a sentence saying what it shows; p12 and p22 fail separately.

results.draft_locus: Processor, Payment Facilitator, Merchant of Record: Who Is the Seller? ¶5

results.finding: The three-role table and the three-panel figure are introduced but no sentence says what they show (that only the merchant-of-record column changes the seller, the statement name and the tax owner); the section ends on the attachments.

results.draft_locus: What to Take Away ¶4
results.quote: Larkfield learned this twice in 2026. On 1 October its renewal job hit a rate limit and 7,900 renewals ran a day late; on 1 November a retry under a new idempotency key charged 1,840 members twice, and €71,300 was refunded.
results.finding: The chapter's conclusion introduces a subtopic the chapter body never discusses (the invoice as the part's organising object, two renewal incidents, Keel's K1/K5) with fresh figures. The spec's conclusion synthesis, callback and takeaway require it as the part's closing.

The conclusion sorts what is established, what depends on context and the author's position, states the invoice synthesis no single section states, and says why it matters (decide fit from who the seller is before a price list; plan the exit).

'The boolean from the opening does not add tax handling to an integration; it replaces the seller' returns to the hook; the 1 October and 1 November 2026 renewals are returned to in What to Take Away ¶4.

The cold reader predicted all seven sections in roadmap order, dated primary-source evidence with figures, the Larkfield case, and a plain, skeptical tone; its open questions are details the body answers.

Reader says A can (automated digital product sold directly) and lists checkout, name on statement/invoice, refund and dispute decisions, part of customer data and the fee; B cannot because salons are the sellers of in-person services through a platform. Matches expected.

Reader gives: processor and payment facilitator leave the business as seller owing the tax; merchant of record is the seller and owes the tax except where local rules prevent transfer. Matches expected.

What to Take Away ¶4 synthesizes Part VI around where the invoice lives and returns to the 1 October and 1 November 2026 renewals; Questions to Ask ¶2 hands off to Part VII through 'Larkfield's studios are the sellers, and they stay the sellers'.

The Adyen reason is labeled inference ('Why it offers no such product is my inference', 'The last column is my inference') while its position is quoted from its 15 September 2026 article; release history is cited to Stripe's changelog and blog ('The release history is in Stripe's own pages'); no sentence says dispute, refund or reversal cost moves to Stripe ('Stripe takes over the work of a dispute, not its cost').
